title: Internal LB staged rollout: Terraform module for TLS termination, health probes, and in-place upgrades
creator: Aditi Rao
description: Create a single, opinionated Terraform module for internal load balancing in Private (VPC) deployments that supports both NLB+TLS passthrough and ALB TLS termination. The module must enable staged/staggered upgrades (zero-downtime where possible), configurable health probes, connection draining, and an easy canary/cutover flow for cert rotation and runtime updates. This is intended for Redwood Private customers who require predictable upgrades and minimal application disruption during Terraform-driven changes.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module published under infra/modules/internal_lb with clear inputs/outputs and examples for: ALB TLS termination, ALB TLS+proxy protocol, NLB passthrough, and hybrid setups.
Support for configurable health_check endpoint (path + port + interval + healthy_threshold + unhealthy_threshold) with option to use TCP vs HTTP/HTTPS checks.

Built-in rolling change strategy: (1) create new target group and listeners, (2) register canary targets, (3) validate using smoke tests and health checks, (4) shift traffic, (5) drain old targets and remove. Documented and executable via terraform apply + module variable toggles.
Automated smoke test (bash/python) that runs after terraform apply and validates: successful TLS handshake, expected response on /_healthz, and metrics sanity (latency within target).
Runbook and rollback steps checked into docs/runbooks/internal_lb_upgrade.md and linked from module README.
Module has backwards-compatible defaults so existing Private stacks can upgrade with minimal changes and a toggle to opt-in to staged rollout behavior.
Integration tests in CI that run against a dev VPC to validate ALB and NLB flows and assert zero-request-loss during a simulated cert rotation.
Security review completed for TLS termination in ALB mode and for KMS integration of cert private keys (security_review_required = true).
design_notes: Prefer ALB for HTTP/HTTPS termination and built-in path-based routing, use NLB for TCP passthrough and lowest latency; module exposes boolean 'terminate_tls' and 'use_nlb'.

Staged rollout implemented via 'desired_phase' variable: plan -> canary -> promote -> cleanup. Each phase maps to Terraform operations that create new resources and reassign target group attachments instead of in-place modifications that cause connection resets.
Health checks default to HTTP /_healthz on port 8080 but are configurable. For services behind TLS termination, ALB can probe HTTP on the target port; for passthrough NLB use TCP health checks.
Connection draining respects 'deregistration_delay' and we add additional graceful_shutdown_seconds to the service to avoid dropped in-flight requests during cert swap.
Module will emit outputs for listener_arn, target_group_arns, nlb_dns_name, alb_dns_name and a webhooks map for external automation to trigger smoke tests.
We will not attempt to manage customer certificates inside module; instead accept ACM cert ARN for ALB or provide pointer to KMS/HSM-managed private certs for NLB TLS listener where required.
Decision: use lifecycle.create_before_destroy on listeners where safe, and opt-in to force replacement only when explicitly requested via input to avoid accidental downtime.
Trade-offs: full zero-downtime cannot be guaranteed for all customer topologies (sticky sessions + legacy clients). Document these limitations and provide fallback a/b toggles.
tasks: Draft Terraform module skeleton with variables, providers, and example instantiations
Implement ALB listener and target group resources with configurable TLS certificate ARN and path-based routing example
Implement NLB listener option for TCP passthrough with cross-zone enabled flag
Add canary workflow variables and plan/apply example scripts (ci/canary-deploy.sh)
Create smoke-test script that validates TLS handshake and /_healthz responses
Add integration tests in CI and a nightly job to validate module against a dev VPC
Write README, runbook, and migration notes for existing Private stacks
Open implementation PR and iterate based on Security/Infra review
